purpose: Define fail-closed conditions before MouldMaster item statistics, cut scores or credentials are interpreted as psychometrically validated.

currentAuthority.currentPassPolicy: at least 80% overall and zero wrong safety-critical regional items

precisionRules: Report item difficulty with an uncertainty interval; target 95% interval half-width no greater than 0.10 before calling the estimate stable enough for operational calibration.
Report discrimination with an uncertainty interval or bootstrap interval; do not call the estimate stable if the interval is too wide to support the intended keep/revise/retire decision.
Retain distractor frequencies, omission rate, response-time distribution, repeat-exposure status and safety-critical error patterns by item revision.
itemAnalysisGate.boundary: The numeric response floor is a conservative planning minimum, not a universal psychometric theorem. Higher samples may be required for extreme item difficulty, subgroup/fairness analysis, adaptive use or high-stakes decisions.

requirements: Use a separately governed summative blueprint with adequate sampling in every claimed competency domain.
Estimate score reliability/precision and uncertainty using methods appropriate to the form and intended decision.
Evaluate dimensionality/construct representation before interpreting one total score as a single competence scale.
Check score consequences, misclassification risk and safety-critical mastery separately from overall score.
testLevelGate.boundary: No reliability coefficient or total-score precision estimate from synthetic traffic, developer accounts or the 8-15 exploratory pilot can satisfy this gate.

requirements: Define the competence claim and target population before standard setting.
Use a documented standard-setting method with qualified independent subject-matter and assessment reviewers.
Report uncertainty/sensitivity around the proposed cut score.
Confirm that the final assessment samples the claimed content domain adequately.
Do not treat the current 80% learning-completion policy as empirical evidence for a professional competence standard.
Review item functioning and outcomes for relevant groups only where ethically collected real data and adequate sample sizes permit defensible inference.
Complete real assistive-technology validation for the assessment interaction itself.
Investigate material accessibility or language barriers before attributing score differences to learner competence.

reviewerTypes: safety reviewer for jurisdiction-specific critical content
